{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZXEUWQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhC-YYg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 39, "title": "Implement Ap real-mode SMSW machine-status readback", "body": "## Problem

Ap stops on `SMSW` (`0F 01 /4`), preventing guest software from querying machine status before choosing a real-mode or protected-mode initialization path. This is a bounded prerequisite following the completed GDTR/IDTR work; it does not require implementing protected execution.

## Expected outcome

Implement Ap real-mode SMSW with CPU-local machine-status readback, correct register/memory widths, addressing, reset and restartable faults.

Hardware contract:

- SMSW copies the machine status word, CR0 bits 15:0, to its destination without changing flags. Register and memory destinations are valid. See [Intel 80386 PRM, SMSW](https://www.scs.stanford.edu/05au-cs240c/lab/i386/SMSW.htm).
- Memory destinations receive exactly two little-endian bytes with either operand size. A word-register destination preserves its upper half. For operand32 register destinations, Intel specifies undefined upper 16 bits; preserve those bits as a documented deterministic emulator policy. LOCK raises exception 6. See [Intel SDM, SMSW, printed pp. 4-647–648](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/782151/253667-sdm-vol-2b.pdf#page=649).
- Expose reset MSW `0010h`: ET set; PE, MP, EM, TS and NE clear. Choose zero for reserved low-word bits as an explicit emulator policy. Follow [Intel486 PRM §10.1, Figure 10-2](https://manuals.plus/m/d86207aaebd9b10464f2058efc61559e6141d3b072db100e89bfe17c8187e143). ET readback does not establish working x87 support.
- Address size independently controls effective-address calculation. Preflight both destination bytes. For this target-era instruction, follow the Intel486 PRM SMSW real-address table, printed p. 26-268: an operand extending beyond `FFFFh` raises exception 13, including SS-selected operands. Explicitly document that the modern SDM instead lists exception 12 for SS overruns; do not describe the tables as agreeing.

Scope is SMSW and the minimum status representation needed for its readback. Guest status writers, MOV control-register instructions, LMSW, CLTS, protected execution, paging and x87 execution remain outside this Issue. Preserve VM's V30 decoder and existing unsupported behavior for other unimplemented instructions.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `dbd65302d2dea6fe6cc22d5dcd356bd3a292b2df`.

Source inspection establishes the missing behavior:

- [Cpu::extended](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/dbd65302d2dea6fe6cc22d5dcd356bd3a292b2df/src/cpu.rs#L663) accepts only Group 7 selectors `/0`–`/3`; `/4` returns `unimplemented i486 opcode 0F 01 /4` before operand decoding.
- [The existing rejection test](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/dbd65302d2dea6fe6cc22d5dcd356bd3a292b2df/tests/cpu386.rs#L961) explicitly includes `/4`. Replace that expectation with positive SMSW coverage while retaining the other rejection assertions.
- Reproduce using the existing `cpu()` helper with bytes `0F 01 E0` (`smsw ax`). Currently `step()` returns the unsupported error. After implementation, AX must contain `0010h`, its upper half must remain intact, and execution must continue without changing flags.
- The current Group 7 implementation assumes a six-byte memory operand. SMSW needs its own register/two-byte-memory handling. The generic memory helper also distinguishes SS faults, so it cannot silently determine this instruction's chosen target-era exception contract.

Project progress: [PR #38](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/38) is recorded as merged. The [Coordinator's validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/dbd65302d2dea6fe6cc22d5dcd356bd3a292b2df/docs/validation.md#issue-37-ap-real-mode-idtr-and-interrupt-table-relocation-2026-10-23) reports 14 focused IDTR passes, 133 native integration passes and 52 production-Wasm browser passes using alternate ports. These were not executed by this evaluator; separate PR reviews and confirmed CI success were not supplied. No open Issues were supplied, and SMSW is distinct from improvements #29–#38.

All 26 inventory categories retain their supplied statuses and full required scopes:

- **Partial:** cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, keyboard, mouse, fdc, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, bios, lio, integration.
- **Unimplemented:** paging, fpu, rtc.
- **Implemented, unverified:** ide, grcg, pcm86.

Protected-mode work still includes CR0/PE entry and exit, descriptor lookup/caches/validation, CPL and privilege transitions, protected gates, LDTR/TR and task-state behavior. CPU exception/restart coverage also remains incomplete. SMSW acceptance will not verify those behaviors or establish commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement the stated contract in original Rust. Read from one CPU-local status representation; construction and Machine reset restore the documented value. Keep changes limited to this behavior and its validation.
- [ ] Add original `smsw_` tests in `tests/cpu386.rs`. Cover all eight register destinations, nonzero upper halves, operand/address-size combinations, repeated overrides, ModR/M/SIB, default SS, segment overrides, unaligned stores, exact destination width, guards and preserved flags/unrelated state.
- [ ] Test the last valid memory start `FFFEh`, invalid `FFFFh`, and address32 offsets `10000h` and `FFFFFFFFh` for DS and SS. Verify the selected exception vector, no partial destination writes, saved first-prefix IP, six-byte real-mode frame, and successful repair/IRET/retry. Test LOCK on register and memory forms with restartable exception 6. Keep general memory-fault behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Verify existing Bus/A20 mapping and ROM write protection for SMSW stores, CPU-instance isolation and reset readback. Preserve GDTR/IDTR acceptance and VM rejection of `0F 01`.
- [ ] Add an original MIT `guest/smsw.asm` boot probe, offline `tools/prepare_smsw_fixture.py`, and checked-in manifest recording source/license, assembler command, source/image hashes, expected bytes/guards and execution budget. Require explicit `SMSW PASS`, no `FAIL` or host error, exact results and unchanged disk bytes within 2,000,000 scheduler slots per boot. Include register/memory readback, operand-size memory guards and guest-handled faults.
- [ ] Run that identical source-built image natively and through the production release Wasm artifact in `tests/browser/smsw.spec.js`, at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, before and after Machine reset. Wire fixture preparation into CI. Keep generated fixtures outside publication assets.
- [ ] The Coordinator records a minimal original test failing on the unchanged baseline with the `/4` diagnostic and passing on the implementation. No baseline implementation substitution or assertion weakening.
- [ ] After preparing the repository's original/licensed fixtures with recorded provenance, pass `python3 tools/prepare_smsw_fixture.py`, `cargo test --locked --test cpu386 smsw_`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `python3 tools/build_media.py --check`, `python3 tools/build_font.py --check`, and `npm test`. Preserve existing hardware, CPULEVEL, DOS/apps, VM and game regressions. Newly introduced guest code must be original or built from explicitly identified licensed source; no commercial ROM/firmware acquisition.
- [ ] Update hardware/compatibility documentation and the validation record with exact commands, outcomes, provenance, specification choices and remaining scope. Do not promote any whole inventory category to verified from this limited acceptance.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
